name: Setup Walkthrough
description: Agent-driven first-time setup playbook that walks new Nomeda users through Obsidian, Atlassian credentials, default module selection, and the SCM-sidebar widgets.

autoOfferOnFreshInstall.label: Auto-Offer On Fresh Install
autoOfferOnFreshInstall.description: When on, TPM detects fresh-install state at session start and offers the walkthrough proactively. When off, the user must explicitly ask (walk me through setup). On is the typical default for new users.

stages.label: Stages
stages.description: User-managed list of walkthrough stages. Each entry is a stage name plus what TPM covers in that stage. Default seeds match the core Nomeda setup; reorder, add, disable individual stages without removing them.

obsidian.value: Confirm or set the Obsidian vault path. Walk through tool.obsidian-notes' auto-discovery toggle and the projectsSubfolder convention.

atlassian.value: Walk through integration.atlassian-suite credential setup — Jira email, API token in SecretStorage, Jira base URL, Bitbucket workspace.

modules-default-set.value: Tour the Modules tab. Highlight which modules are default-enabled and which are opt-in. Suggest the typical-workflow toggles based on whether the user does ticket work, PR review, or both.

scm-widgets.value: Point out the Branch Widget and Ticket Widget in the Source Control sidebar. Explain when each appears (Atlassian Suite enabled / Ticket Work mode + ticket id set).

first-session.value: Suggest a low-stakes first session — open a small ticket in Ticket Work mode, watch the AC extract into todos, run the pre-PR trio on a real change. The user learns by doing, not by reading.

freshInstallSignal.label: Fresh Install Signal
freshInstallSignal.description: How TPM detects fresh-install state. no-prior-handoff treats the absence of any Session Handoff blocks in the Obsidian vault (or the vault not being resolved) as fresh-install. empty-feedback-log treats an empty feedback log as the signal. always-offer offers the walkthrough at every session start regardless (useful for testing). manual-only never auto-offers — only fires on explicit ask. Default no-prior-handoff is reliable when tool.obsidian-notes is enabled.

paceMode.label: Pace Mode
paceMode.description: How TPM walks through the stages. interactive walks one stage at a time, waiting for user input or completion before moving on. linear walks all stages in one long output; user reads through and acts as needed. self-paced surfaces the full stage list and lets the user pick which to do first. Default interactive is the most-supportive for first-time users.

completionTracking.label: Completion Tracking
completionTracking.description: When on, TPM records which stages the user completed (or skipped) so the walkthrough isn't re-offered on subsequent sessions. When off, the walkthrough re-offers based purely on the freshInstallSignal each session. On is recommended; off is for testing the walkthrough repeatedly.
